name: Question 9
problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ be a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y={X}_{1}-2{X}_{2}.$
worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y=a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of $a$ and $b,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & =a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2}, \\ Var[Y] & ={a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+2ab{\sigma }_{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have ${\mu }_{1}=0$ and ${\mu }_{2}=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[{X}_{1}-2{X}_{2}] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}_{1}]-2\text{E}[{X}_{2}] \\  & ={\mu }_{1}-2\cdot {\mu }_{2} \\  & =0-2\cdot (1) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we have ${\sigma }_{1}^{2}=1,{\sigma }_{2}^{2}=4,$ and ${\sigma }_{12}={\sigma }_{21}=1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Var[Y] & =Var[{X}_{1}-2{X}_{2}] \\  & ={1}^{2}\cdot 1+(-2)^{2}\cdot 4+2\cdot 1\cdot (-2)\cdot 1 \\  & =1+16-4 \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(-2,13).
$$

Question 9
?

Let X=[X1,X2]T be a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector μ and covariance matrix Σ given by μ=[01],Σ=[1114]. Find the distribution of Y=X1−2X2.

a
Y∼N(−2,17)
b
Y∼N(−2,15)
c
Y∼N(−2,13)
d
Y∼N(−2,17)
e
Y∼N(−2,13)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if X=[X1,X2]T is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector μ and covariance matrix Σ, given by μ=[μ1μ2],Σ=[σ12σ12σ21σ22], then the random variable Y, defined as

Y=aX1+bX2

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of a and b, where

E[Y]=aμ1+bμ2,Var[Y]=a2σ12+b2σ22+2abσ12.

In our case, we have μ1=0 and μ2=1. Therefore,

E[Y]=E[X1−2X2]=E[X1]−2E[X2]=μ1−2⋅μ2=0−2⋅(1)=−2.

Also, we have σ12=1,σ22=4, and σ12=σ21=1. Therefore,

Var[Y]=Var[X1−2X2]=12⋅1+(−2)2⋅4+2⋅1⋅(−2)⋅1=1+16−4=13.

Therefore, we conclude that

Y∼N(−2,13).
